title: Geo-containment playbook and immutable audit bundles for Private/VPC residency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers using Private/VPC or on-prem deployments require a provable containment model for data jurisdiction and retention during regional evacuations and graceful failover. Existing controls surface where data lives but do not produce tamper-evident, exportable evidence bundles for auditors, nor do they encode regional exit constraints as executable policies. This ticket scopes a pragmatic engineering deliverable: a Geo-Containment Playbook (operational runbook + machine-readable policy) and an Immutable Audit Bundle exporter that automates evidence collection (residency assertions, retention settings, KMS key access logs, network egress proofs) when a regional failover or evacuation is initiated.
acceptance_criteria: A0: A machine-readable policy schema (JSON) that can express: allowed regions, emergency-exit-allowed boolean, max-retention-override per-customer, acceptable-fallback-regions list, and required audit artifacts to collect.

A1: Automation that, when a region-evacuation event is triggered, collects a signed, timestamped bundle containing: residency assertions for all customer-backed VMs/instances, retention configuration snapshots, KMS access audit trail for the last 90 days, NAT/eBPF-based egress proof logs, and a service-level routing decision record.

A2: Bundles are generated as immutable artifacts (content-addressed namespace, SHA256 checksums) and written to a customer-specified object store or a temporary WORM area; a human-readable summary is included with cryptographic verification steps.
A3: The system emits a single canonical report ID per-event and surfaces it in Console (Private control plane) with links to the artifact and minimal metadata for compliance reviewers.
A4: End-to-end test that simulates a region failover in a staging VPC and validates that the bundle contains all required artifacts and that checksums verify after transfer.
A5: Security review completed and PRD sign-off from PM and Legal for wording to ship to customers.
A6: Performance: evidence collection must not exceed 12 minutes for an average customer footprint (<= 25 instances) in the staging runbook test.
A7: Role-based access to generated artifacts enforced (only customer admins and Redwood auditors can access) and access events are logged.
A8: Backwards-compatible with existing residency assertion endpoints and can be toggled per-customer via the Private control plane feature flag.
A9: Documentation: playbook runbook published (Confluence link) and Console UI copy updated.
work_notes: 2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting with PM (Sofia Becker), Legal (E. Nguyen) and Infra SRE. Agreed scope: policy schema + collector + immutable export. High-level deadlines set.

2026-03-06: Spike executed to evaluate options for immutable storage: S3 Object Lock (customer-provided) vs. internal content-addressed archival. Early preference for content-addressed bundles to avoid cross-account permission complexity.
2026-03-08: Prototype script collects residency assertions and retention config from control plane; identified gaps: KMS audit ingestion requires additional work (ENG-18093 referenced).
2026-03-09: Met with Console team to design how canonical report ID surfaces in Private control plane. Agreed to place initial link in Activity > Compliance section.
2026-03-11: Security review queue submitted; threat model call scheduled. Raised concern about bundling KMS logs that contain internal metadata — legal asked for redaction heuristics.
2026-03-12: Performance run for 18-instance test completed: bundle creation 7m42s. CPU and network hotspots identified; will parallelize collection tasks and stream checksums to reduce latency.
2026-03-13: Implementation branch created (github.com/redwood/infra/PR#5124). Initial unit tests added for policy schema validation.
checklist: Define policy JSON schema and publish to specs repo
Integrate KMS access logs ingestion and redaction rules
Implement content-addressed bundle creation and checksum signing
Add Console hooks to display report ID and artifact link
Complete security review and legal approval
Add e2e staging test and perf benchmarks
test_plan: Unit: policy schema validation and negative tests for malformed policies.
Integration: collector runs against a staging VPC that mimics a medium customer (20 instances, 2 subnets). Verify collected artifacts are present and signed.
E2E: Trigger simulated region evacuation; verify bundle creation time < 12 minutes and Console surfaces report link.
Access controls: attempt artifact download as non-admin user and expect 403.
Data integrity: transfer bundle to customer object store and re-validate SHA256 checksums match original.
Regression: ensure existing residency assertion endpoints remain unaffected by the collector.
Load: run 5 parallel evacuation simulations for small customers to ensure collector scales horizontally.
